intro.paragraph: I design, build and run web applications in TypeScript, from enterprise integrations to the ticketing platform of a race I founded. I work from the first requirement to production, with an architecture that stays readable and a delivery that stays calm, so that teams can focus on what matters.

engineering.title: Engineering
engineering.lead: Complete products, from the database to the interface.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
infrastructure.lead: From commit to production: automated tests, images and Kubernetes deployments.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.lead: Shipping as a team without wearing down the architecture.
notes: Short sprints and regular reviews: the team ships in small steps and corrects course fast. PSM I certified.
The business logic sits at the centre, isolated from the database and frameworks by ports and adapters. Easier to test and to evolve.
Five principles to keep code readable: one responsibility per class, open to extension, inverted dependencies.
Small, independent services deployed separately. Practised in a monorepo on the JCDecaux applications.
Break down, estimate, order: know what ships and when, and say so as soon as it slips.
